record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.original_question:
Given a subset Ω of the complex plane and π(Ω), the class of all
univariate polynomials whose zeros all lie in Ω,
characterize all linear operators T such that T maps every polynomial
in π(Ω) either to another polynomial whose zeros
still all lie in Ω or to the zero polynomial.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Characterize all linear operators T : π(Ω) → π(Ω) ∪ {0}. Let πn denote the vector space (over R or C) of all polynomials of degree ≤ n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a given subset of the complex plane. Denote by $\pi(\Omega)$ the class of all univariate polynomials with complex coefficients all of whose zeros lie in $\Omega$ (with the convention that constant nonzero polynomials, having no zeros, belong to $\pi(\Omega)$ vacuously). For each integer $n \ge 0$, let $\pi_n$ denote the vector space (over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$) of polynomials of degree at most $n$.

Characterize explicitly all linear operators $T$ acting on the polynomial ring (or on $\pi_n$ for each $n$) with the following zero-location preserving property: for every $p \in \pi(\Omega)$, the image $T(p)$ is either the zero polynomial or again belongs to $\pi(\Omega)$.

That is, give a complete description of the family
$$\bigl\{\, T : T\bigl(\pi(\Omega)\bigr) \subseteq \pi(\Omega) \cup \{0\} \,\bigr\}$$
for an arbitrary prescribed region $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is fully solved in several important cases but remains open for general $\Omega$. Borcea and Brändén (2009) gave a complete characterization when $\Omega$ is an open circular domain or its closure (including the upper half-plane, giving the stability/Hurwitz case, and the real line). Subsequent work has extended the characterization to strips and to interval-rooted polynomials (Brändén–Chasse and others). A characterization for arbitrary $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is not known.

status_evidence.title: The Lee-Yang and Pólya-Schur Programs. I. Linear Operators Preserving Stability
status_evidence.snippet: Borcea and Brändén characterize all linear operators on polynomials preserving non-vanishing in prescribed open circular domains.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization is known for open circular domains (including stability/upper half-plane case).

status_evidence.title: Classification theorems for operators preserving zeros in a strip
status_evidence.snippet: Classification theorems for operators preserving zeros in a strip.
status_evidence.claim: The problem has been addressed and solved for strips, extending Borcea–Brändén.

status_evidence.title: A Representation Theoretic Explanation of the Borcea-Brändén Characterization, and an Extension to Interval-Rooted Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Extends Borcea–Brändén to characterize a subclass of linear operators preserving polynomials with roots in a real interval or ray.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extensions exist for interval-rooted polynomials, but a general-$\Omega$ characterization is not given.
